clue.text: Leading actors, high-pitched?

blocks.note: a team that is leading is up, ahead in the score
the actors in a production are its cast

explanation.surface: A review praising the stars of a play while sniping that their voices were shrill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High-pitched' looks like a comment on voices, but pitched here means thrown, and the question mark flags that cricket-style sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Something upcast has been flung or directed upwards, so it was literally thrown on high.

clue.text: Hold up for quick inspection

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: to hold something is to keep it

explanation.surface: Something is held aloft so that people can have a brief look at it.
explanation.definitionFit: A peek is a brief furtive glance, a short look taken quickly at something.

clue.text: Vegetable in a healthy establishment, with sauces added

blocks.note: taken as written
a spa is a resort or centre visited for health treatments
ragus are rich Italian meat sauces

explanation.surface: A health resort's menu offers a green vegetable drowned in sauces.
explanation.walkthrough: A ragu is the Italian meat sauce served with pasta; its plural sits after A SPA.
explanation.definitionFit: Asparagus is a green spear-shaped plant whose young shoots are eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Bouncer putting two grand in bank

indicators.note: putting one thing in another places it inside, so the pair goes within the bank

blocks.note: a bank of seats or oars is a tier, a row
G is short for grand, a thousand pounds; two of them

explanation.surface: A nightclub doorman stashing two thousand pounds in the bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bouncer' suggests a doorman, but it is the bouncy tiger from Winnie-the-Pooh.
explanation.definitionFit: Tigger, the tiger friend of Winnie-the-Pooh, is famous for bouncing about on his springy tail.

clue.text: Superficial harm resulting from friction among climbers

definitions.text: Superficial harm resulting from friction among climbers

blocks.note: surface reading: a skin graze caused by rubbing, perhaps friction between people
setter's reading: the injury mountaineers get when a cord runs fast across the skin

explanation.surface: Mountaineers squabbling, with the friction between them causing only minor hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Friction among climbers' reads like a row in the team, but it is literal rubbing of their lines on skin.
explanation.definitionFit: This injury is a skin abrasion caused when a cord slides quickly across the body, a typical climbing mishap.

clue.text: Rule, as stated, over Persians, Afghans, and others – come down hard on all

indicators.note: as stated means as spoken, so the word for rule is taken by its sound

blocks.note: to rule is to reign, which is said just like the weather word
Persians are a breed of cat, Afghans a breed of hound, and these with the rest make up household pets of both kinds

explanation.surface: A ruler cracking down on everyone, from Persians and Afghans to all the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: Persians and Afghans look like peoples of the Middle East, but here they are a cat breed and a dog breed. 'Over' puts the first part above the rest in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To rain cats and dogs is an idiom for pouring with heavy rain, falling hard on everyone.

clue.text: Terriers in pub still running amok

indicators.note: running amok is wild disorder, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Dogs are still tearing around the pub causing chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: The pit bull is a muscular fighting breed of the terrier group, bred originally for baiting.

clue.text: Early problem raised in land of cats?

indicators.note: raised in a down entry means lifted to read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: a.m. denotes the morning, the early part of the day
a rub is a difficulty, as in 'there's the rub'

explanation.surface: A trouble from long ago comes up again in the place where cats come from.
explanation.walkthrough: The Burmese is a breed of cat, hence the playful definition with its question mark; the country is now Myanmar.
explanation.definitionFit: Burma, now Myanmar, gives its name to the Burmese breed, so it is jokingly the home country of those pets.

clue.text: Those mortified by bad cluemanship? They’re still aware of grouse

blocks.note: first meaning: puzzle compilers blushing with embarrassment at poor clues
second meaning: gundogs that freeze motionless when they scent game birds

explanation.walkthrough: 'Grouse' looks like a complaint from a solver, but it is the game bird; setters are dogs that stand still on finding one.
explanation.definitionFit: Blushing compilers would be scarlet-faced setters, and the Irish breed of gundog is the familiar chestnut-coated pointer of birds.

clue.text: Piano included in arrangement of eg Irish or Italian composer

indicators.note: included in means placed inside, so the musical letter sits within the rest
an arrangement puts things in a fresh order, so these letters are reordered

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
p is the musical marking for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A piano part is worked into a medley of Irish or Italian tunes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irish or Italian' seems a choice of nationalities; only Italian belongs to the definition, and 'or' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Ottorino Respighi was an Italian composer, best known for the orchestral tone poems on Rome's pines and fountains.

clue.text: Extended rant from one caught in traffic

indicators.note: something caught in something else is trapped inside it

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
traffic in goods is trade, buying and selling

explanation.surface: A driver stuck in a jam launches into a long angry outburst.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Traffic' conjures cars, but it is dealing in goods, as in drug traffic.
explanation.definitionFit: A tirade is a long angry speech of denunciation, a sustained verbal attack.

clue.text: Doctor agreed on cure – given new heart

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are altered in order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A physician settles on a treatment, a heart transplant for the patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New heart' sounds like transplant surgery, but heart here means courage.
explanation.definitionFit: To be re-encouraged is to have one's courage or spirit restored, heart meaning confidence.

clue.text: Does try to outrun these pursuers

definitions.text: Does try to outrun these pursuers

blocks.clueFragment: Does try to outrun these pursuers
blocks.note: surface reading: a question of whether someone attempts to escape their chasers
setter's reading: does are female deer, and the chasers are the large hounds bred to hunt them

explanation.walkthrough: 'Does' reads as the verb opening a question; it is the plural of doe, and the hunting dogs are named for their quarry.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish deerhound is a tall rough-coated sighthound bred for coursing red deer.

clue.text: Accumulation of ice in December gales

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the following words, spanning them

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the month and the start of the winds

explanation.surface: Ice building up in the winter storms of December.
explanation.definitionFit: A berg, short for iceberg, is a huge floating mass of ice broken off a glacier.

clue.text: Campanological scandal? Pay to get through it

blocks.note: campanology is bell-ringing, and a bell's slow ringing is a toll
-gate is the suffix tagged onto scandals since Watergate

explanation.surface: A bell-ringers' scandal, and a demand for money to make it go away.
explanation.walkthrough: Campanology is the art of bell-ringing; the scandal suffix comes from Watergate.
explanation.definitionFit: A tollgate is a barrier across a road that opens only once the traveller has handed over a fee.

clue.text: Breed in Grand National from Europe

blocks.note: grand and great both mean large and impressive
a Dane is a national of Denmark, a European country

explanation.surface: A horse in the Grand National that was bred on the Continent.
explanation.walkthrough: The Grand National is Britain's famous steeplechase horse race, which makes 'Breed' look equine; the two words are taken separately.
explanation.definitionFit: The Great Dane is a breed of very large dog, originally German despite the name.

clue.text: Infamous criminal better placed in solitary

indicators.note: placed in means set inside, so one word goes within the other

blocks.note: solitary means on one's own
to better someone is to cap or top their effort

explanation.surface: A notorious gangster would be better off locked in solitary confinement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solitary' suggests a prison cell, fitting the gangster, but it simply means by oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: Capone was the Chicago gangster of the Prohibition era, eventually jailed for tax evasion.

clue.text: Herb and I coming across right area for capital

indicators.note: coming across means straddling, so the first pair spreads around the single letter

blocks.note: basil is a culinary herb
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: Herb and I cross the right part of town on our way to the capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Herb' could be a man's name travelling with the speaker; it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Brasilia is the purpose-built capital city of Brazil, inaugurated in 1960.

clue.text: His jumble is included by Disraeli – for instance!

definitions.text: His jumble is included by Disraeli – for instance!

indicators.note: only what is included by the name is kept, so its outer letters are shed
a jumble is a muddled heap, so the letters come out in another order

blocks.note: the statesman's surname, whose inner letters are kept

explanation.surface: A remark that a statesman's own rank is mixed up in his name, Disraeli being an example.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: Benjamin Disraeli was made Earl of Beaconsfield, so he is an instance of the title hidden in his own name.
explanation.definitionFit: An earl is a British nobleman, and Disraeli was ennobled as Earl of Beaconsfield in 1876.

clue.text: Like certain animals in pounds and ounces, say

definitions.note: an example of the animals the adjective describes, not an adjective itself

blocks.note: first meaning: resembling the cats, as opposed to dogs, found in animal shelters
second meaning: the ounce is the snow leopard, a big cat

explanation.walkthrough: Pounds and ounces look like imperial weights; here a pound is an animal shelter and an ounce is the snow leopard.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means belonging to the cat family, which takes in stray cats and snow leopards alike.

clue.text: Measure concealing dishonest statements about firm is most unwise

indicators.note: concealing means hiding inside, so the outer word wraps the rest
about means around, so the lies wrap round the word for firm

blocks.note: a foot is a unit of length
untrue statements are lies
firm and hard both mean solid

explanation.surface: A policy that covers up corporate lies is the height of folly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a company, but it is the adjective, solid.
explanation.definitionFit: Foolhardy means recklessly bold, so the superlative describes the most rashly unwise choice.

clue.text: Pioneer space-traveller left, otherwise called about one

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the alias abbreviation goes round the numeral

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
aka stands for 'also known as'
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An early astronaut who departed and went by another name.
explanation.walkthrough: Laika was the Soviet dog launched on Sputnik 2 in 1957, fitting the puzzle's dogs and cats theme.
explanation.definitionFit: The Soviet dog was the first animal to orbit the Earth, a true pioneer of space travel.

clue.text: Male you tease audibly, fool

indicators.note: audibly means as heard, so the words are replaced by letters with the same sound

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for male
the letter U is pronounced like this pronoun
the word is said like the plural of the letter T, so more than one of that letter

explanation.surface: A man taunting someone out loud and calling them an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: Tease sounds like 'Ts', the plural of the letter, read here as a pair. The answer is also a mongrel dog, in keeping with the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A mutt is informal for a stupid or incompetent person, as well as a mongrel.

clue.text: Colour used finally in my opening statement?

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before it
in places that letter inside the statement that follows

blocks.note: what one might announce on opening a door and entering: 'In I go'
the final letter of used

explanation.surface: A speaker wonders whether a particular colour was the last word in their opening remarks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening statement' suggests a speech or a trial; the question mark flags the literal sense of a remark made while opening a door to go in.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigo is a deep blue-violet hue, one of the seven colours of the rainbow.

clue.text: Plant one in Guardian, perhaps, with indication of hesitancy

indicators.note: in places the numeral inside the newspaper word

blocks.note: a newspaper such as the Guardian is an organ, a publication voicing views
the Roman numeral for one
um is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: Someone hesitantly suggests placing a plant in this very newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guardian' looks like a protector, but this puzzle appears in the Guardian, a newspaper, and papers are called organs.
explanation.definitionFit: Origanum is the botanical genus of aromatic herbs that includes oregano and marjoram.

clue.text: Like English author, they check for flaws in material

definitions.text: they check for flaws in material

blocks.note: like and as both mean in the manner of
Dorothy L. Sayers, English writer of the Lord Peter Wimsey mysteries

explanation.surface: Like a novelist, editors scour the material for mistakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Material' suggests a writer's manuscript, but it is metal or ore being tested.
explanation.definitionFit: Assayers test metals and ores to determine their purity and content, finding any impurities.

clue.text: Stuff thrown out from jet ace reassembled

indicators.note: reassembled means put together again differently, so the letters take a new order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A fighter pilot's plane is rebuilt after he ejects, debris scattered about.
explanation.definitionFit: Ejecta is material expelled, especially from a volcano or an impact crater.
